protein: RNase III (rnc), the double-stranded RNA endoribonuclease
readout: Growth fitness relative to wild-type synonyms
assay_method: Site-saturation library of the whole rnc coding region on plasmid pRnc2-gGFP, transformed into rnc-minus E. coli SK7622 and grown for 10 generations of exponential growth in LB. Fitness w_i = ln(r*eps_i)/ln(r*eps_wtsyn) from the change in mutation frequency before and after growth, pooled over synonymous codons, reported as the variance-weighted mean of two replicas.
remark: The reference sequence is the 226-residue rnc coding region printed as the column header of the source matrix, byte-identical to UniProt P0A7Y0. There is no WT row: the source matrix leaves the wild-type residue blank at every position, wild type being the normalizing reference rather than a measured cell. wt_readout is 1 by the definition of w_i, which divides through by the wild-type synonym rate, rather than by measurement. The 225 nonsense measurements are dropped, a stop codon not being a substitution in this format. The article PDF could not be retrieved and is not redistributed in papers/: PMC serves an HTML interstitial in its place and the publisher returns 403, so only the open supplementary files are staged. Not extracted from this paper: the codon-level tables of Supplementary Data S4, S6 and S8, which measure the same variants at a finer granularity than this format carries; the per-replica columns, since the weighted mean is the value the paper analyses; and the k* alignment values of Supplementary Data S10, which are computed rather than assayed.

protein: RNase III (rnc), the double-stranded RNA endoribonuclease
readout: log10 enrichment ratio on transformation, relative to wild-type synonyms
assay_method: The same site-saturation library, transformed out of rnc-plus NEB5-alpha into rnc-minus E. coli SK7622. The transformation score is the log of the enrichment of a mutant relative to the enrichment of alleles synonymous for wild type, so a score of -1 is a 10-fold depletion in the SK7622 library. A single measurement, not replicated.
remark: The reference sequence is the 226-residue rnc coding region printed as the column header of the source matrix, byte-identical to UniProt P0A7Y0. There is no WT row: the source matrix leaves the wild-type residue blank at every position, wild type being the normalizing reference rather than a measured cell. wt_readout is 0 because the score is a log ratio against wild-type synonyms, which is 0 by construction. The 225 nonsense measurements are dropped, a stop codon not being a substitution in this format. The article PDF could not be retrieved and is not redistributed in papers/: PMC serves an HTML interstitial in its place and the publisher returns 403, so only the open supplementary files are staged. This readout is the only one of the three with no replicate structure in the source, so it carries no weighted mean and no per-replica spread. Not extracted from this paper: the codon-level table of Supplementary Data S6, and the k* alignment values of Supplementary Data S10, which are computed rather than assayed.

protein: FabZ, the 3-hydroxyacyl-ACP dehydratase of fatty acid biosynthesis
readout: Competition coefficient over 15 generations of growth
assay_method: Saturation mutagenesis of the chromosomal copy of the gene by CRISPR base editing in E. coli, so the gene stays under its native regulation and copy number, followed by competitive growth for 15 generations with library composition read by direct edit detection on the genome. The competition coefficient is the slope of a weighted least-squares log-linear fit of each edit's abundance over the time course, computed with Enrich2, normalized to total read counts and shifted so the most common coefficient is zero.
remark: The reference sequence is UniProt P0A6Q6 unmodified, against which all 2358 mutation labels for this gene verify at offset 0. The WT row is the mean of the 139 synonymous edits, which the library carries as its own internal controls rather than defining wild type as zero; those 139 measurements span -0.988 to 1.041, which is the clearest statement of the assay's reproducibility this source offers, and their mean of 0.0006 lands near the zero the normalization targets. The 637 edits for which the source records no coefficient are dropped. Not extracted from this paper: the read-count tables of Supplementary Data 1 to 3, which are the counts this coefficient is fitted from rather than a phenotype; the per-residue tolerance scores of Supplementary Data 5, which summarize these same variants one position at a time rather than one variant at a time; and the antimicrobial resistance hits of Supplementary Data 6, which are a list of mutations recovered from resistance screens with a count of how often each was found, not a scored library.
